# `silk/u64`

<!-- Generated by packages/compiler/scripts/generate-documentation.mjs. Do not edit by hand. -->

Sixty-four-bit unsigned integers for wide masks, counters, hashes, and exact interchange values.

## When to use

Use `u64` when a stable unsigned 64-bit representation matters. It is the representation used
for hash output; use `usize` instead for target-sized collection lengths and indices.

## Details

Ordinary arithmetic, narrowing conversions, division by zero, and invalid shift counts trap.
`checked*` returns [`Option`](./option.md#declaration-73696c6b2f6f7074696f6e3a3a4f7074696f6e), `wrapping*` computes modulo 2^64, and `saturating*` clamps at
[`MIN`](#declaration-73696c6b2f7536343a3a4d494e) or [`MAX`](#declaration-73696c6b2f7536343a3a4d4158). Right shift inserts zero bits.

Decimal [`parse`](#declaration-73696c6b2f7536343a3a7061727365) consumes the complete input and separates malformed text from range overflow.
[`toText`](#declaration-73696c6b2f7536343a3a746f54657874) allocates owned text. Conversion to a floating type may round large values.

## Gotchas

A `u64` can represent values that neither `i64` nor every target's `usize` can hold; use a
checked conversion when that boundary is controlled by input.

Import as `u64` with `import silk.u64`.

Public declarations: 57.
